chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said:

A son of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) died, and he was informed of his death. So he ordered that he be washed and shrouded, and he walked with him and prayed upon him. A prayer mat was placed, so he stood upon it, then he stood at his grave until he finished, then he departed, and I departed with him until I was walking alongside him.

So he said: 'Indeed, Salat was not performed upon one like this, and he was a boy of three years old. Ali (peace be upon him) used to order that he be buried and Salat not be performed upon him, but the people did something, so we do similar to it.'
He said: I said, 'So when is Salat obligatory upon him?' So he said: 'When he has intellect for Salat, and is a boy of six years old.'

I said, 'So what do you say regarding the children?' So he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about them, so he said: Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing funeral prayer for children in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential evolution of funeral prayers for children, distinguishing between the Imams' traditional practice of burying young children without prayer and their later adoption of the community's custom for those aged six and above. It highlights the theological principle that for pre-discernment children, divine knowledge of their individual deeds supersedes ritual formalization, a nuance rooted in the Prophet's response to inquiries about the 'wildan' (young boys).
